audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart and the prose disagree about level 6. win[4] and phases[4] give Level 6 to Lillia and whys[4] says she edges it, while spikes[1].text, mid and wants.you[1] all say 6 is the stage where 'everything flips' to Camille because the arena beats her kiting. One of the two is wrong and I did not guess which.
audit.why: 47.97% over 296 games is an unfavoured lane overall, so a Lillia-sided level 6 is defensible; but the page's own strongest claim is that The Hextech Ultimatum is 'the one tool her whole kit fears'. Both cannot stand.
audit.corrected: Left the chart and the prose exactly as they are and raised it in questionsForUser instead of inventing a power shift.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her spikes are described as 'free-casting Swirlseed and her Q dash' with no cooldowns, so 'wait until her E is down' had no number. Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s, Swirlseed a flat 12s, Watch Out! Eep! 14s, Lilting Lullaby 150/130/110s.
audit.why: Cooldowns from champ-data/_kits/lillia.json. Swirlseed's flat 12s is the one that matters: it is her only real ranged tool and it does not get shorter with ranks, so the 12s after she throws it is the window your wall-E is keyed to.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, mid and wants.foe[0] now carry Swirlseed's flat 12s and Blooming Blows' 6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabricated mechanics, repeated across nine strings. (1) 'Her Q dash' / 'Q-dashes away' / 'can't Q-dash out' - Blooming Blows is not a dash. It is a self-centred AoE that deals extra TRUE damage on its outer edge and passively stacks move speed when her spells hit. Her mobility is that stacking speed, not a blink. (2) 'E-roll' - Swirlseed is a seed she throws that rolls along the ground until it hits something; she does not roll. (3) 'heal off Q' / "Q's self-heal" - Blooming Blows has no heal in Riot's text at all. Also missing: Lilting Lullaby only drowses enemies who already have Dream Dust on them, so if she has not landed a spell on you her ult does nothing to you. Camille's Hookshot is called a stun throughout; Riot says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot, Blooming Blows: 'Passively, Lillia gains stacking Move Speed when hitting enemies with spells. She can activate this to deal magic damage to nearby enemies, dealing extra true damage on the edge.' Swirlseed: 'Lillia hurls a seed that damages and slows those it lands on. If it doesn't hit anything, it will continue rolling until it hits a wall or target.' Lilting Lullaby: 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.'
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3], early, mid, late, whys[2..4] and the wants entries now describe stacking move speed instead of a dash, a thrown rolling seed instead of a roll, no Q heal, and the Dream Dust precondition on her ult.

edits.before: Lillia owns level 1 with passive Dream Dust burn and Swirlseed (E) poke while you have one ability and no all-in, so don't walk up — last-hit and respect the chip. Your window is 2-3: take E early, and the moment a wall is near, Hookshot in and land your Q-recast for the true-damage second hit before she Q-dashes away and resets distance. Don't try anything fancy here — just punish the instant she steps up to last-hit, because her base damage can't out-trade your Q recast when you actually stick to her.
edits.after: Lillia owns level 1 with Dream Dust burn and Swirlseed (E) poke while you have one ability and no all-in, so don't walk up — last-hit and respect the chip. Your window is 2-3: take E early, and the moment a wall is near, Hookshot in and land your Q-recast for the true-damage second hit before her stacked move speed resets the distance. Swirlseed is a flat 12s at every rank, so the seed leaving her hands starts your clock. Punish the instant she steps up to last-hit — her base damage can't out-trade your Q recast when you stick to her.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are her best window: she free-casts E (Swirlseed) and weaves her Q dash to stack passive Dream Dust burn and heal off Q while your E is on cooldown and you can't reach her. Eat the poke with your Adaptive Defense shield up and wait for 6. At 6 everything flips — Hextech Ultimatum is the one tool her whole kit fears, because it cages her in an arena she can't Q-dash or E-roll out of and her sleep R can't disengage from inside, so chain E-into-R and delete her in the isolation before she ever spaces you.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are her best window: she free-casts Swirlseed (E, flat 12s) and weaves Blooming Blows (Q, 6s) to stack Dream Dust burn and pile up move speed while your E is down and you can't reach her. Eat the poke with your Adaptive Defenses shield up and wait for 6. At 6 your Hextech Ultimatum is the one tool her kit fears, because stacked move speed buys nothing inside the arena — and Lilting Lullaby only drowses enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so staying clean of her spells blanks it outright.

edits.after: She free-casts Swirlseed on its flat 12s and weaves Blooming Blows for Dream Dust burn and speed while your E is down — her best poke window.

edits.after: Even past 6, stacked Blooming Blows speed and the Swirlseed slow reset distance between your dives faster than you can re-close once your E is spent — she edges the extended trades.

edits.before: This is where she reclaims it. Full-build AP Lillia is exactly the mobile, slippery skirmisher your dive struggles to pin: she kites your gap-close with Q movement speed and E slows, her sleep R hard-disengages your all-in or sets up a return, and her Dream Dust burn plus magic damage out-values you at even items. Your job is to have already won — snowball off your level-3 wall window and the 6 all-in, end on tempo, and never let the game become a spaced-out duel where she scales past you.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as Lillia steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. Great trade: Lillia uses or whiffs Blooming Blows: instantly E off a wall for the stun and attack-speed surge, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit, W to heal, and R to isolate him if he tries to run. Bad trade: Burning Hookshot (E) aggressively, missing the stun, and getting stuck in a drawn-out melee grind while your E and shield are down. That is how Camille loses a winning lane.

edits.before: Your E-stun off a wall into the empowered Q2 is a premium gank setup — ping your jungler when E is up and Lillia's escape is down. You are most vulnerable right after you E in with it on cooldown, so ward the river bush before you dive.

notes: Three invented mechanics here, all repeated: a 'Q dash' (Blooming Blows is a self-centred AoE with true damage on the edge and passive stacking move speed - no dash anywhere), an 'E-roll' (Swirlseed is a thrown seed that rolls, not a Lillia roll), and a 'Q self-heal' that does not exist in Riot's text. A player who reads 'wait for her Q dash' will hold E for a blink that never comes. The genuinely useful replacement is the Dream Dust precondition on Lilting Lullaby: no Dream Dust on you, no drowsy, no sleep. _missing-interactions.json claims Lillia can cancel The Hextech Ultimatum via Lilting Lullaby, on the strength of a 'channel' flag in camille.json - but Riot's own text for Camille's R describes a dash and an anchor with no channel, and the drowsy has a delay before the sleep lands, so I did NOT write that cancellation. Logged as unverified.
